entries.test: Compare publicly documented scaling gains, training and operating costs, and LLM revenues through August 2025 with the predictions in Marcus's August 2023 essay.
entries.note: The claim that his essay anticipated the present implicitly endorses its account of diminishing returns and economic difficulties.
“Immense disappointment” expresses an evaluation without specifying a promised capability or measurable shortfall.
“Nobody is buying” is sweeping rhetorical exaggeration, not a literal claim about every person's belief.

entries.test: Compare Altman's public remarks in the week before August 18, 2025 with his earlier statements about AGI's proximity and importance.
entries.note: Marcus asserts an interpretation of Altman's public statements in his own voice. The embedded “may” describes the concession he attributes to Altman.
“The best” ranks unlike applications of deep learning without a shared criterion of merit.

entries.test: Examine public evaluations available by August 18, 2025 for whether any deep-learning approach reliably solved general reasoning, hallucinations, elementary errors, or factual accuracy.
entries.note: “Other” and “either” include LLMs in the contextual claim that these problems remain unsolved. Success on a narrow task would not establish a general solution.

entries.test: Examine public performance trends through August 18, 2025 for whether existing deep-learning techniques had plateaued on reasoning, hallucinations, elementary errors, and factual accuracy.
entries.note: The principal assertion is a present plateau, qualified by the possibility of a new technique. Its plain reading is stronger than merely saying the problems remain unsolved.

entries.test: Compare public competitive evaluations of OpenAI and public assessments of Altman's credibility before and immediately after GPT-5's release to determine whether both declined while OpenAI retained a lead.
entries.note: The context supports reading “his lead” as OpenAI's competitive lead. “After” establishes sequence without necessarily asserting causation.

entries.test: Compare Altman's public promises with GPT-5's demonstrated capabilities and his subsequent public statements to determine whether delivery fell short and he lowered expectations.
entries.note: The normalization omits the additional assertion that Altman is seeking to remain relevant. The retained claim about unmet promises and public expectation lowering is checkable.
